subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app adopt a chat-first default or mode, or should OpenClaw only accept focused Android chat/media/connection improvements while keeping the current Home-first companion shell?
rationale: Current main has much of the Android chat foundation, but the remaining decision changes user-facing navigation, setup expectations, media scope, and mobile product positioning.

options.title: Accept focused slices only
options.body: Keep the Home-first Android shell for now and invite small PRs for specific chat/media/connection improvements with real device proof.

options.title: Sponsor chat-first design
options.body: Open or designate a focused design issue that defines the chat-first mode/default, navigation, media scope, security constraints, and validation bar before implementation.

options.title: Decline official direction
options.body: Close the official-app discussion and point fork authors to maintain separate Android clients unless a narrow core API gap is identified.

recommendation.title: Accept focused slices only
recommendation.body: Keep the Home-first Android shell for now and invite small PRs for specific chat/media/connection improvements with real device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Android chat features and current-main Android shell/docs blame make this the best available routing owner for the product-direction choice.
